None of the three solutions is convincingly correct, so I'm choosing NONE, though I can't rule out that 15 is the true value.

**Solution 2 (∞) is wrong.** Its argument checks the wrong condition. A vector field preserves D when [X, Γ(D)] ⊂ Γ(D), not when X commutes with the generators. The proposed field a(y₁₂, y₁₃)∂_{y₁₂} + b(y₁₂, y₁₃)∂_{y₁₃} does not commute with e₁, e₂, e₃. Each e_i has a ∂_{y₁₂} or ∂_{y₁₃} component with x-dependent coefficient, so [e_i, X] picks up terms like c_i(x)·∂a/∂y₁₂ ∂_{y₁₂}, which are generally not in D. Bracket-generating distributions of constant growth also have finite-dimensional symmetry algebras (Tanno/Tanaka theory), so ∞ cannot be right.

**Solution 1 (21) is unsupported.** It is a guess from a B₃ parabolic that is never tied to the growth vector (3,6,8) or to the grading dimensions (3,3,2). Its own reasoning wavers ("so(4,4)", "so(8,ℂ)", "B₃") before settling on 21 without a check.

**Solution 3 (15) is plausible but not established.** The 8-dimensional nilpotent algebra is valid: I checked the Jacobi identities, and the growth is (3,6,8). The symmetry count of 8 right-invariant fields plus 7 symbol automorphisms is asserted rather than derived. The 7-dimensional stabilizer is not verified to be the full graded automorphism algebra preserving V. The maximality claim, that the symbol automorphisms bound everything, is also unjustified, since symmetry algebras of non-flat or non-graded models can be larger. I could not check the literature for this specific growth type, so I cannot confirm 15.

CHOICE: NONE
